5274-the-chaplet-of-pearls.creator: Charlotte M. Yonge
5274-the-chaplet-of-pearls.description: A book by Charlotte M. Yonge. here are some which only attempt to portray human feelings as affected by the events that such warfare occasioned. ‘Old Mortality’ and ‘Woodstock’ are not controversial tales, and the ‘Chaplet of Pearls’ is so quite as little.

arxiv-2004-08770.title: Energy Storage Optimization for Grid Reliability
arxiv-2004-08770.creator: Md Umar Hashmi, Deepjyoti Deka, Lucas Pereira, Ana Bušić
arxiv-2004-08770.description: Abstract Large scale renewable energy integration is being planned for multiple power grids around the world. To achieve secure and stable grid operations, additional resources/reserves are needed to mitigate the inherent intermittency of renewable energy sources (RES). In this paper, we present formulations to understand the effect of fast storage reserves in improving grid reliability under different cost functions.

arxiv-2104-00674.title: PhySG: Inverse Rendering with Spherical Gaussians for Physics-based Material Editing and Relighting
arxiv-2104-00674.creator: Kai Zhang ∗, Fujun Luan ∗, Qianqian Wang, Kavita Bala, Noah Snavely, Cornell University
arxiv-2104-00674.description: Abstract We present PhySG, an end-to-end inverse rendering pipeline that includes a fully differentiable renderer and can reconstruct geometry, materials, and illumination from scratch from a set of RGB input images. Our framework represents specular BRDFs and environmental illumination using mixtures of spherical Gaussians, and represents geometry as a signed distance function parameterized as a Multi-Layer Perceptron.

arxiv-2105-00129.title: WfChef: Automated Generation of Accurate Scientific Workflow Generators
arxiv-2105-00129.creator: Tainã Coleman 1 , Henri Casanova 2 , Rafael Ferreira da Silva 1
arxiv-2105-00129.description: Abstract Scientific workflow applications have become mainstream and their automated and efficient execution on large-scale compute platforms is the object of extensive research and development. For these efforts to be successful, a solid experimental methodology is needed to evaluate workflow algorithms and systems. A foundation for this methodology is the availability of realistic workflow instances.

arxiv-2108-03886.title: Do Images really do the Talking? Journal: Applied Intelligence
arxiv-2108-03886.creator: Siddhanth U Hegde, Adeep Hande, Ruba Priyadharshini, Sajeetha Thavareesan, Ratnasingam Sakuntharaj, Sathiyaraj Thangasamy, B Bharathi, Bharathi Raja Chakravarthi
arxiv-2108-03886.description: Abstract A meme is an part of media created to share an opinion or emotion across the internet. Due to its popularity, memes have become the new forms of communication on social media. However, due to its nature, they are being used in harmful ways such as trolling and cyberbullying progressively.

arxiv-2110-03382.title: Analysis of the influence of political polarization in the vaccination stance: the Brazilian COVID-19 scenario
arxiv-2110-03382.creator: Régis Ebeling, Carlos Abel Córdova Sáenz, Jeferson Nobre, Karin Becker
arxiv-2110-03382.description: Abstract The outbreak of COVID‐19 had a huge global impact, and non-scientific beliefs and political polarization have significantly influenced the population’s behavior. In this context, COVID vaccines were made available in an unprecedented time, but a high level of hesitance has been observed that can undermine community immunization.

arxiv-2112-14339.title: Non-Relativistic Supergeometry in the Moore -Read Fractional Quantum Hall State
arxiv-2112-14339.creator: Patricio Salgado-Rebolledo, Giandomenico Palumbo
arxiv-2112-14339.description: Abstract The Moore-Read state is one of the most well known non-Abelian fractional quantum Hall states. It supports non-Abelian Ising anyons in the bulk and a chiral bosonic and chiral Majorana modes on the boundary. It has been recently conjectured that these modes are superpartners of each other and described by a supersymmetric conformal field theory Ma et al.

arxiv-2305-19367.title: Fibration symmetries and cluster synchronization in the
arxiv-2305-19367.creator: Caenorhabditis elegans
arxiv-2305-19367.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Caenorhabditis elegans. Abstract

Capturing how the
Caenorhabditis elegans
connectome structure gives rise to its neuron functionality remains unclear. It is through fiber symmetries found in its neuronal connectivity that synchronization of a group of neurons can be determined. To understand these we investigate graph symmetries and search for such in the symmetrized versions of the forward and backward locomotive sub-networks of the
Caenorhabditi elegans
worm neuron network.

arxiv-2406-07085.title: CAT: Coordinating Anatomical-Textual Prompts for Multi-Organ and Tumor Segmentation
arxiv-2406-07085.creator: Zhongzhen Huang, Yankai Jiang, Rongzhao Zhang, Shaoting Zhang ✉, Xiaofan Zhang ✉
arxiv-2406-07085.description: Abstract Existing promptable segmentation methods in the medical imaging field primarily consider either textual or visual prompts to segment relevant objects, yet they often fall short when addressing anomalies in medical images, like tumors, which may vary greatly in shape, size, and appearance.

arxiv-2407-09204.title: Electron bubbles in highly excited states of the lowest Landau level
arxiv-2407-09204.creator: David D. Dai, Liang Fu
arxiv-2407-09204.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by David D. Dai, Liang Fu. We study the entire energy spectrum of an electron droplet in the lowest Landau level. By exact diagonalization calculations, we find highly excited states in the middle of the spectrum that display unexpected density distribution and pair correlation. We show that these exceptional excited states contain tightly bound electron bubbles with local filling ν = 1 \nu=1 that form various ordered structures.

arxiv-2412-14077.title: Dialogue with the Machine and Dialogue with the Art World: Evaluating Generative AI for Culturally-Situated Creativity
arxiv-2412-14077.creator: Rida Qadri, Piotr Mirowski, Aroussiak Gabriellan, Farbod Mehr, Huma Gupta, Pamela Karimi, Remi Denton
arxiv-2412-14077.description: Abstract This paper proposes dialogue as a novel and experimental qualitative method for evaluating generative AI tools for culturally-situated creative practice. Drawing on sociologist Howard Becker’s concept of Art Worlds , this method expands the scope of traditional AI and creativity evaluations beyond benchmarks, user studies with crowd-workers, or focus groups conducted with artists.

arxiv-2503-18377.title: Maximum Redundancy Pruning: A Principle-Driven Layerwise Sparsity Allocation for LLMs
arxiv-2503-18377.creator: Chang Gao, Kang Zhao, Jianfei Chen, Liping Jing
arxiv-2503-18377.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities, but their enormous size poses significant challenges for deployment in real-world applications. To address this issue, researchers have sought to apply network pruning techniques to LLMs. A critical challenge in pruning is allocation the sparsity for each layer.

arxiv-2506-15652.title: A Machine Learning Framework for Modeling Ensemble Properties of Atomically Disordered Materials
arxiv-2506-15652.creator: Zhenyao Fang, Ting-Wei Hsu, Qimin Yan
arxiv-2506-15652.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhenyao Fang, Ting-Wei Hsu, Qimin Yan. Disorder, though naturally present in experimental samples and strongly influencing a wide range of material phenomena, remains underexplored in first-principles studies due to the computational cost of sampling the large supercell and configurational space. The recent development of machine learning techniques, particularly graph neural networks (GNNs), has enabled the efficient and accurate predictions of complex material properties, offering promising tools for studying disordered systems.

arxiv-2510-16393.title: Blending Learning to Rank and Dense Representations for Efficient and Effective Cascades
arxiv-2510-16393.creator: Franco Maria Nardini, Raffaele Perego, Nicola Tonellotto, Salvatore Trani
arxiv-2510-16393.description: Abstract . We investigate the exploitation of both lexical and neural relevance signals for ad-hoc passage retrieval. Our exploration involves a large-scale training dataset in which dense neural representations of MS-MARCO queries and passages are complemented and integrated with 253 253 hand-crafted lexical features extracted from the same corpus.

arxiv-2511-12622.title: IR/UV mixing from higher-order interactions in a Scalar Field
arxiv-2511-12622.creator: Satish Ramakrishna
arxiv-2511-12622.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Satish Ramakrishna. The mismatch between the observed vacuum energy and the value suggested by quantum-field-theoretic estimates is a foundational puzzle. While Lorentz-invariant regularization softens the naive quartic divergence, it still leaves a discrepancy of many orders of magnitude and appears incompatible with Weinberg’s no-go theorem, which prohibits obtaining a small cosmological constant within local, translationally invariant quantum field theory (QFT) without fine tuning. One broad class of ideas that can evade these constraints involves nonlocal or quasi-nonlocal assumptions that induce UV/IR limit mixing.

arxiv-2602-22086.title: MBD-ML: Many-body dispersion from machine learning for molecules and materials
arxiv-2602-22086.creator: Evgeny Moerman, Adil Kabylda, Almaz Khabibrakhmanov, Alexandre Tkatchenko
arxiv-2602-22086.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Evgeny Moerman, Adil Kabylda, Almaz Khabibrakhmanov, Alexandre Tkatchenko. Van der Waals (vdW) interactions are essential for describing molecules and materials, from drug design and catalysis to battery applications. These omnipresent interactions must also be accurately included in machine-learned force fields. The many-body dispersion (MBD) method stands out as one of the most accurate and transferable approaches to capture vdW interactions, requiring only atomic C 6 C_{6} coefficients and polarizabilities as input.

pmc-10547909.title: How Nurses’ Person-Organization Fit Influences Organizational Loyalty
pmc-10547909.creator: Miaomiao Sun, Fahad Alam, Cunxiao Ma
pmc-10547909.description: BackgroundHigh turnover rates among nurses are a global concern due to the shortage of skilled professionals and increasing demand for high-quality healthcare. This study aims to enhance understanding of organizational fit by examining the impact of Person-organization fit (P-O fit) on organizational loyalty through the mediating role of organizational support and service quality, and the moderating impact of role ambiguity.

pmc-10632337.title: Spontaneous orientation polarization of flavonoids
pmc-10632337.creator: Kouki Akaike, Takuya Hosokai, Yutaro Ono, Ryohei Tsuruta, Yoichi Yamada
pmc-10632337.description: Spontaneous orientation polarization (SOP) is macroscopic electric polarization that is attributed to a constant orientational degree of dipole moments of polar molecules on average. The phenomenon has been found in small molecules like H2O at low temperatures and π-conjugated molecules employed in organic light-emitting diodes.

pmc-10670582.title: Definition and Criteria for the Assessment of Expertise in Psychotherapy: Development of the Psychotherapy Expertise Questionnaire (PEQ)
pmc-10670582.creator: Alessio Gori, Eleonora Topino, Marco Cacioppo, Adriano Schimmenti, Vincenzo Caretti
pmc-10670582.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Therapist expertise is a complex, multifaceted, and continually evolving concept. Defining this construct and its constituent components can yield a substantial contribution to the field of psychotherapy, consequently enhancing the comprehension of the fundamental factors that underlie its effectiveness. Within this framework, the present research aimed at developing and assessing the psychometric properties of the Psychotherapy Expertise Questionnaire (PEQ), a self-report measure to assess therapist expertise. A sample of 260 psychotherapists of various theoretical orientations were involved in this research.

pmc-11539585.title: Myocardial blood flow in newly diagnosed breast cancer patients at rest and during exercise
pmc-11539585.creator: Tiia Koivula, Tytti-Maria Uurasmaa, Chunlei Han, Teemu Maaniitty, Shiva Latifi, Salla Lempiäinen, Kari Kalliokoski, Carl Johan Sundberg, Helene Rundqvist, Katja Anttila, Heikki Minn, Juhani Knuuti, Ilkka Heinonen
pmc-11539585.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryThe heart depends critically on continuous blood supply, but it is unknown whether cancer itself affects myocardial blood flow (MBF). This study investigated MBF in cancer patients and cardiac morphology in a cancer mice model. MBF was quantified with [15O]H2O positron emission tomography at rest in recently diagnosed breast cancer patients and age-matched female controls, and additionally during 10-min exercise in the cancer patients. Cardiac morphological changes were analyzed with a breast cancer mouse model and control mice without tumors.

pmc-11593123.title: Feasibility of Non-Invasive Sentinel Lymph Node Identification in Early-Stage NSCLC Through Ultrasound Guided Intra-Tumoral Injection of 99mTc-Nanocolloid and Iodinated Contrast Agent During Navigation Bronchoscopy
pmc-11593123.creator: Desi K. M. ter Woerds, Roel L. J. Verhoeven, Erik H. J. G. Aarntzen, Erik H. F. M. van der Heijden
pmc-11593123.description: Simple SummaryThis clinical feasibility study explored the use of a novel device that integrates radial ultrasound and an angulated needle to inject 99mTc-nanocolloid and CT contrast for visualization of the sentinel lymph nodes (SLN) using SPECT and CBCT imaging. Radial ultrasound could visualize 29 out of 30 tumors. Injection of imaging tracers was feasible in all patients.

pmc-12364098.title: A one-pot strategy for the synthesis and functionalization of hyperbranched polytriazoles
pmc-12364098.creator: Hyeongju Noh, Jaehyeon Kim, Jina Min, Se Yeon Cheon, Si Kyung Yang
pmc-12364098.description: Herein we report a one-pot strategy for the synthesis and functionalization of hyperbranched polytriazoles by means of the Huisgen 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition of an AB2-type monomer containing an alkyne and two azide groups. The AB2 monomer is synthesized starting from dimethyl 5-hydroxyisophthalate in four steps with an overall yield of 58%, and the synthesis and purification are straightforward.

pmc-12554820.title: A comparison of isolated mandibular fractures and pattern of fractures of the mandible in cases with panfacial fractures – A study from 2007 to 2024 in a highest-level German trauma centre on 2056 patients with mandibular fractures
pmc-12554820.creator: Lars Bonitz, Leonie Koch, Stefan Hassfeld, Ákos Bicsák
pmc-12554820.description: IntroductionThis study investigates mandibular fractures focusing on long-term trends and fracture patterns of mandibular fractures as isolated fractures and as part of panfacial fractures.MethodsIn addition to descriptive demographics, the fracture site distribution was statistically compared with the Wilcoxon rank test and compared in groups with the χ2-test.

pmc-12759300.title: Collection of Ambulatory Electrocardiogram and Behavioral Data for the Identification of Digital Biomarkers for Heart Failure (CATCH-ECG): Protocol for a Prospective Cohort Study
pmc-12759300.creator: Jakob Eyvind Bardram, Gouthamaan Manimaran, Chloë Cammaerts, Sadasivan Puthusserypady, Helena Dominguez, Javad Sarvestan, Neelam Gupta
pmc-12759300.description: BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is a complex clinical syndrome with a high morbidity and mortality rate. Despite advancements in treatment, the recurrence of HF remains a significant challenge, often leading to deteriorating health conditions and increased pressure on the health care system. Early detection of recurrence is pivotal in mitigating and managing the adverse outcomes associated with HF.

pmc-12991845.title: Low-dose biochar and nitrogen fertilizer reduces nitrogen loss in acidic tea soils
pmc-12991845.creator: Cenwei Liu, Jing Ye, Yi Lin, Bangwei Zhang, Weixi Shu, Yixiang Wang
pmc-12991845.description: SummaryExcessive nitrogen fertilizer in red-soil tea plantations reduces quality and yield in southern China and causes environmental issues. This study employed 15N isotope tracing to evaluate the effects of co-applying biochar (0%, 1%, 2%, and 4%) with nitrogen fertilizer on tea growth, nitrogen use efficiency (NUE), and soil microbial communities in acidic red-soil plantations.

pmc-13321632.title: Unrecognized ciliary motility disorders in neutrophilic severe asthma exacerbations
pmc-13321632.creator: Sarita Thawanaphong, Lucia Gonzalez-Bravo, Katherine Radford, Melanie Kjarsgaard, Carmen Venegas Garrido, Sergey Fedosenko, Terence Ho, Lindsey Dyment, Nadia Suray Tan, Kayla Zhang, Adil Adatia, Manali Mukherjee, Myrna Dolovich, Parameswaran Nair
pmc-13321632.description: BackgroundAirway bacterial infections are frequent in severe asthma and are often under-appreciated as contributors to symptoms and exacerbations. We report our experience using integrative diagnostic methods to identify ciliary motility disorders as contributors to neutrophilic exacerbations in patients with severe asthma.

pmc-13385894.title: Spatial memory performance is associated with region-specific coordination of hippocampo-cortical sleep oscillations
pmc-13385894.creator: Mauricio Caneo, Nelson Espinosa, Alejandro Aguilera, Guillermo Lazcano, Ariel Lara-Vasquez, Pablo Fuentealba
pmc-13385894.description: Sleep plays a critical role in memory consolidation, yet how coordination among sleep oscillations across hippocampo-cortical circuits relates to behavioral performance remains incompletely understood. Here, we examined how cross-regional coordination of cardinal sleep oscillations during non-rapid eye movement (nREM) sleep relates to spatial memory performance.
